free_tier.stated: 1 hostname on a No-IP shared domain, no credit card; the hostname must be confirmed every 30 days or it is deleted

per_object_cap.stated: 1 hostname on the free plan, on one of 30+ No-IP shared domains; the zone belongs to No-IP, so the user holds no record count of its own; hostnames may be type A, AAAA or Port 80 Redirect

retention.stated: a free hostname is active for 23 days, may be confirmed in the next 7 days, stops resolving when it expires, sits 14 more days in redemption and is then deleted and open to anyone; an update from a client does not confirm it
retention.notes: confirmation is a web login or an e-mailed link

egress.terms: no DNS query cap published on the pages read

interface_detail: a dyndns2-style HTTP update request, GET https://dynupdate.no-ip.com/nic/update?hostname=HOST&myip=IP with HTTP Basic auth (the account e-mail address and password), on port 443 over HTTPS or on ports 80 and 8245 over HTTP; the response is a text code such as good, nochg or badauth; the pages read list a RESTful API only under the contact-sales Branded Remote Access plan
tooling: the free No-IP Dynamic Update Client for Windows, macOS and Linux, any dyndns2-compatible client or router, and curl from cron; confirmation itself is a web or e-mail action with no documented API
chaining: a name for a changing address and nothing else on the free plan; the domains are No-IP's, so the name cannot be a zone of its own, and the 30-day confirmation has to be done by hand

limits.value: confirm every 30 days: active 23 days, 7-day confirmation window, 14-day redemption, then deletion

binding_note: the 30-day manual confirmation is what decides; an update client keeps the address current but does not renew the hostname

identity_cost.detail: the sign-up form asks for an e-mail address and a password and a terms checkbox that states one free account; the free page says no credit card is required (https://www.noip.com/sign-up, https://www.noip.com/free); no phone field in the captured form text

reliability_note: a free hostname silently stops resolving if the 30-day confirmation is missed; the update endpoint answers HTTP 401 with the body badauth for a request without credentials; a client without an approved User-Agent can be rate-limited or blocked, and the badagent and abuse codes tell a client to stop updating
confidence_note: the free-plan page, the confirmation knowledge-base page, the FAQ, the sign-up page and the update protocol pages were read and quoted; the unauthenticated update endpoint was probed once and answered 401 badauth
